closest_prior_work.citation: Brown et al. (2025). AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data. arXiv:2507.22291.
closest_prior_work.difference: Evaluates AlphaEarth for mapping and biophysical prediction from sparse labels; this paper instead tests whether its distance adds value for same-vegetation NWI water-regime reference matching beyond physical covariates.

closest_prior_work.citation: Feng et al. (2025). TESSERA: Temporal Embeddings of Surface Spectra for Earth Representation and Analysis. arXiv:2506.20380.
closest_prior_work.difference: Introduces a global optical/SAR embedding model covering 2017–2024; this paper uses one TESSERA product as a matching distance rather than evaluating general representation learning.

closest_prior_work.citation: Ryan et al. (2026). Streamlining Wetland Vegetation Mapping with AlphaEarth Embeddings. Remote Sensing, 18(2), 293.
closest_prior_work.difference: Finds embedding-based wetland vegetation mapping comparable to traditional workflows; the endpoint here is matching an inventory water regime for a reference wetland, not classifying vegetation.

closest_prior_work.citation: Qu et al. (2026). Utilizing Earth Foundation Models to Enhance the Simulation Performance of Hydrological Models with AlphaEarth Embeddings. arXiv:2601.01558.
closest_prior_work.difference: Reports that embedding similarity identifies hydrologically comparable donor basins and improves ungauged-basin simulation; this paper tests an analogous similarity idea at individual-wetland scale against NWI labels and physical pair models.

closest_prior_work.citation: Liu et al. (2026). Geospatial Foundation Embeddings as Transferable Catchment Descriptors. Geophysical Research Letters.
closest_prior_work.difference: Shows AlphaEarth embeddings can be functionally comparable to traditional catchment attributes for rainfall–runoff prediction; this paper asks the narrower incremental question for wetland inventory-category screening and finds the increment unattributable under its controls.

main_issues.issue: Temporal and endpoint mismatch: 2024 annual embeddings are mostly evaluated against NWI regimes whose source imagery is ≤2014 for 2,756 of 3,667 primary wetlands, and the endpoint is interpreted inventory agreement rather than measured hydroperiod or reference suitability.

The primary equal-window estimand is fragile: windows range from 18 to 890 queries, two windows contribute 19 accepted queries yet dominate the AlphaEarth change, pooled effects are much smaller, and window-bootstrap intervals omit forest-seed and label uncertainty.

Attribution remains only a descriptive qualification, not a formal test: there are just three planned permutations, no permutation p-value or matched permutations for the later six seeds, and random-forest dimension changes alone can move results by amounts comparable to the claimed increment.

The own-screen metric conflates better reference ranking with different query selection; on the fixed hydrological screen the AlphaEarth ranking component is only -0.52 of the -2.95 pp total, so the operational interpretation is weaker than the headline contrast suggests.

The physical baseline is not a decisive strongest comparator: it lacks explicit SAR inundation, soil and gauge information, and polygon-averaging the same physical maps or using all-feature forests materially changes or beats several augmented comparisons.

Generality is narrow: 12 convenience windows, nine NWI code combinations, NWI-derived polygons and vegetation controls, old labels, and an unexecuted independent geographic replication frame do not support US-wide, open-set or field-reference conclusions.

Reproducibility from the paper alone is limited because the referenced research directory, VERIFY.md, sources.jsonl, analysis files and window coordinates are not given a public repository, DOI or URL in the manuscript.

Presentation is heavily overloaded with dozens of exploratory learners, transforms, years, allocations and appendix conditions, obscuring the single primary result; some appendix table headers are also cramped or overlapping.

research_question.predictable_reason: A small or unstable increment was foreseeable because embeddings overlap terrain and surface-water information and the NWI labels are old and noisy, although the exact seed and permutation comparability required the experiment.
research_question.question: Does adding annual AlphaEarth or TESSERA embedding distance improve wetland reference screening beyond terrain, optical surface-water and drainage covariate matching at fixed coverage when vegetation subclass and geography are controlled?

score_reasons.clarity: Definitions and caveats are careful, but the abstract and 36-page results are overloaded with exploratory contrasts and repeated qualifications that obscure the main takeaway.
score_reasons.correctness: The central claim is conservatively stated as 'not established' and is supported by pooled, fixed-screen, seed, permutation and alternative-learner checks, though the primary metric and temporal design prevent a stronger negative conclusion.
score_reasons.generality: Evidence is confined to convenience US windows, selected palustrine codes, NWI-derived geometry and labels, and two archived embedding products, with no field or independent-frame validation.
score_reasons.novelty: The exact label-masked NWI reference-matching diagnostic and null-feature controls appear new within the searched range, but embedding-based wetland mapping and hydrological similarity selection are already established directions.
score_reasons.usefulness: It usefully warns embedding evaluators that single-seed added-feature gains can be fitting noise, but it offers no validated practitioner workflow or field-hydrology benefit.
score_reasons.verifiability: Hyperparameters, spatial splits, seeds, bootstrap settings and data versions are unusually detailed, yet no accessible repository or window list is identified in the paper and many decisive records are only referenced by local filenames.

strengths: Spatially separated query, reference and training roles with 1 km training exclusion and training-only imputation, scaling and embedding transformations reduce obvious leakage.

The planned seed, embedding-permutation and alternative-learner checks, later supplemented by constant-column and independent-scalar diagnostics, are an unusually transparent way to expose added-feature and random-forest seed fragility.

The paper reports favourable and unfavourable results together, including pooled versus equal-window estimates, tiny-window contributions, fixed-query ranking decompositions and single-window omissions.

Scope is repeatedly and appropriately limited to inventory-label agreement, with explicit warnings that neither embedding similarity nor an NWI match establishes hydroperiod, ecological condition or restoration suitability.
review.summary: The paper asks whether annual AlphaEarth/TESSERA embedding distances improve selection of same-vegetation wetland references with matching NWI water regimes beyond a 30-covariate terrain, surface-water and HAND model. In 3,667 wetlands across 12 convenience windows, seed-0 equal-window mismatch improves by 2.95–3.72 percentage points, but pooled gains are smaller, tiny windows dominate, and planned permutations, seed variation and alternative learners make the increment unattributable under the authors' qualification rule. It is therefore best read as a rigorous, inconclusive-to-negative diagnostic with valuable null-control methodology, not as evidence about field hydroperiod or a usable reference-selection method.
